author: agent:claude-code
message: Re-recording four of this session's journal entries whose text was dropped (passed as 'text' instead of 'body'); each supersedes the empty one.

title: Float maths without std through a &self extension trait
body: core has no sqrt / sin / powi ... for f32 and f64, so the no-std path needs them from libm without changing call sites (x.sqrt() on both paths). units::float_math::FloatMath carries std's whole set under std's names, implemented by the inherent methods with std and by libm without; crate::alloc_prelude brings it into scope only without std. Its methods take &self on purpose: Elementwise and RealValued already give f32 / f64 by-value sqrt, sin, exp ..., and two by-value candidates would be ambiguous (E0034, 125 errors). Method lookup tries by-value before autoref, so where those traits are in scope they win and FloatMath fills in the rest. Consequence: without std, a concrete f32 x.exp() / ln() / tanh() with Elementwise in scope runs fastmath's Cephes kernels (within 2 ulp of std's); f64 is libm either way. The units' own impls call FloatMath::f(&x) by name, which is unambiguous on both paths and can't recurse into the impl. Rejected: renaming the methods (every call site changes, std reads worse); fixing ~130 call sites with cfg; a by-value trait (ambiguous wherever the units traits are in scope).

title: What changes without std, and how it's tested
body: Without std: streams (signal::stream, built on io::Result throughout) are left out, with Source::stream / stream_for and the interop example; Endian moved to signal::storage since DynArray's byte conversion needs it on both paths. Lookup tables built on first use go through units::lazy::Lazy (an AtomicPtr race-once cell; the loser's value is dropped; the made-value path is #[cold] so hot loops keep one load) on both paths instead of OnceLock. Per-thread caches have no thread-locals to live in: array maths plans its FFT per call, BigFloat's default precision is one global (AtomicU32) and its constants aren't cached. AVX2 is used when the build targets it instead of detected at run time. The crate is no_std only when neither std nor test is set: unit tests link std (the harness and the tests need it) while the code under test keeps its no-std paths; cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown is what proves the library itself needs no std. With std nothing was lost: rustdoc's public API (18,590 entries default, 24,052 all features) matches 575bfa2 apart from seven constants shown as core:: instead of std::, the examples' 15 output files are bit-identical, and benchmarks are within 0.95-1.02x.

title: One criterion baseline comparison read load as a 65% regression
body: Checking the std path for regressions, cargo bench with --save-baseline at the old commit and then --baseline on the new reported reverb +65%, waveshaper 4x +38%, slice loop +28% and also fft -17%, Zip transposed -31%, on code that didn't change (the reverbs' diff was one import). Alternating the two built binaries (old, new, new, old ... best of 4) put all 15 within 0.95-1.02x. Lesson: compare two versions by alternating their binaries in one session and taking each side's best, never one baseline run against a later one; a swing in both directions on untouched code is load, not the change. (Also: criterion keeps baselines under the working directory's target/, not --target-dir.)

title: What parda measured building the prototype
body: From parda's graft 01a10a6b (crates/autodyne-math in parda2D at 7912896, divan against glam 0.30, 1,024 values per op): generic over Float works with _ZERO, _ONE, lit, _sqrt, _abs, _min, _max, _sin_cos, _is_finite and UnitOps' operators; types have zero() / identity() since Float has no Default; bytemuck Pod as unsafe impls per concrete type (no padding with repr(C)). f32 SIMD without specialization: TypeId::of::<T>() == TypeId::of::<f32>() then cast to the f32 types and call SSE (SSE2 is baseline on x86-64), compiled away per instance (confirm in the assembly that the f64 instance carries no branch): Mat4 * Mat4 4.27 vs glam 4.30 us, Mat4 * Vec4 600 vs 595 ns. Slower, don't repeat: the SSE single product inside compose_world (17% slower than glam; plain arithmetic is 2% faster: 27.7 vs 28.3 us at 10k), and 16-byte aligned Vec4 (737 vs 600 ns). The gap: Mat4 inverse 9.6 us by scalar cofactors against glam's SSE 7.3 (glam's src/f32/sse2/mat4.rs: 2x2 sub-determinants by shuffles); Mat3 inverse by cross products is already 4% faster. The API parda calls is listed in the graft's point (5), so parda switches by changing one dependency.
